skill.description: Save images, videos, or audio from supported social media links using SocialDataX commands, with source records and download status.
skill.summary: Organize requested social media downloads into local folders with source links, file paths, and failure reports.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: Thirty-six alerts are false positives involving Markdown, Chinese text, service links, or documented credential configuration. Two command locations execute an unpinned npm package without an installation prompt, creating supply chain exposure. No evidence found of malicious intent, credential exfiltration, or prompt injection in the reviewed files; external package behavior was not verified.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md executes socialdatax-skills@latest through npx -y, allowing the resolved package and its dependencies to change between runs.
remediation.suggestion: Use a reviewed, exact package version with locked dependencies and integrity checks. Request approval before first execution and restrict accessible credentials and filesystem permissions.

content.user_title: Save and Organize Social Media Files
content.value_statement: Social media downloads are difficult to track when source links, local files, and failed items become separated. This skill guides SocialDataX downloads and organizes files with source records and explicit results.
actual_capabilities: Guides media saving from Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, X / Twitter, and Bilibili using existing SocialDataX commands.
Distinguishes content pages from direct media URLs and selects relevant media fields from platform detail responses.
Places distinct materials in separate empty subdirectories within the requested output directory.
Deduplicates repeated media URLs while retaining their source references.
Records platform, available content identifiers, source links, local paths, media types, download status, and failure reasons.
Verifies reported download results against actual files and checks source records before accepting skipped existing files.
limitations: Requires external SocialDataX tooling and Node.js/npm; the documented commands execute the latest package version rather than a pinned release.
Online detail lookups and Bilibili download link requests require SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY and may require provider credits.
Bilibili media merging requires ffmpeg; its MCP tool returns download links rather than saving or merging files.
Supports only the documented platforms and available media; network restrictions, unavailable content, or missing media can prevent downloads.

use_cases.title: Collect Approved Campaign Assets
use_cases.description: Save media from an explicit campaign link list and retain source references for each downloaded file.

use_cases.title: Track Research Materials
use_cases.description: Organize media from selected research posts, preserve complete identifiers, and record unavailable materials without inventing results.

use_cases.title: Prepare Editing Materials
use_cases.description: Collect requested images, videos, or audio into separate folders and identify missing files before editing begins.

prompt_templates.title: Save One Media File
prompt_templates.prompt: Save this direct media URL: [media URL]. Use [output directory] and report the verified local path or actual failure reason.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Media From a Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Save the requested [media type] from [supported post URL] into [output directory]. Keep complete source links and exclude unrequested covers or music.
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: resolve a supported content page

prompt_templates.title: Organize Multiple Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Process only these links: [link list]. Save distinct materials under [output directory], deduplicate repeated media URLs, and report successes, failures, and source references.

prompt_templates.title: Resume an Existing Collection
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume this collection using [source manifest] and [link list] in [output directory]. Verify existing file mappings, preserve completed files, and report unresolved items.

output_examples.input: Save two supplied direct media links, including one duplicate, into the selected folder.
output: Illustrative result: one unique file saved and verified in the selected output directory.
The repeated media URL was downloaded once, with both source references retained.
The source list includes the actual returned local path, media type, and verified status.

output_examples.input: Resume a collection where one existing file is verified and another media link is unavailable.
output: Illustrative result: the verified existing file is retained and marked as already present.
The unavailable item remains in the source list with its actual download error.
No successful download or local path is claimed for the failed item.

output_examples.input: Resolve a supplied post when the provider reports insufficient balance.
output: Illustrative result: the lookup stops without repeated retries.
The provider billing link is shown, and previously saved files remain unchanged.
The failed lookup can resume after the account balance is restored.

best_practices: Provide an explicit link list and output directory, and authorize only the requested media and necessary dependency changes.
Review the external package before execution and prefer an approved pinned version in a restricted environment.
Verify downloaded files and source mappings, preserve complete links, and keep API keys out of generated files.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a content page URL as a direct media URL or assume every platform response contains a video.
Do not count a submitted command or an unverified skipped_existing status as a successful new download.
Do not download extra assets, overwrite unrelated files, or expand beyond the supplied links and authorized directories.

faq.question: Which platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The instructions cover Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, X / Twitter, and Bilibili. They do not promise support for other sites.

faq.question: Do direct media downloads require an API key?
faq.answer: Direct download-media operations do not require a key. Online detail lookups and Bilibili download link requests use SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY.

faq.question: What software must be available?
faq.answer: CLI execution requires Node.js/npm and external SocialDataX tooling. Bilibili merging also requires ffmpeg. The documented npm commands use an unpinned latest version.

faq.question: How are existing files and duplicate links handled?
faq.answer: Repeated media URLs are saved once. Existing files count as matching only when source records confirm their identity; otherwise, a new empty subdirectory is used.

faq.question: Can the skill post content or access browser sessions?
faq.answer: The instructions exclude posting, likes, comments, account operations, and browser login data access. They permit requested local downloads and source records.

faq.question: What happens when downloads fail or credits run out?
faq.answer: Successful files are retained and failures are listed with actual reasons. Insufficient balance stops repeated retries and directs the user to provider billing.
